ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure are the positive and negative terminals of the input voltage u_i, and the arrow of current i enters the load from left to right. In the upper branch of the load, it first passes through the inductor L inside the dashed box, then connects to the vertically placed resistor R on the right side, and finally returns to the bottom wire; therefore the image shows that L and R are in a series relationship. When the problem says to short-circuit the inductor inside the dashed box, only resistor R remains in the load path. Reasoning: When the inductor is short-circuited, only R=50Ω bears the input voltage. Given i_short=2sin(ωt−15°) A, the input voltage u_i=R i_short=50×2sin(ωt−15°)=100sin(ωt−15°) V. When the inductor works normally, the series impedance Z=R+jX_L=50+j50=50√2∠45° Ω. Dividing the input voltage phasor by the impedance phasor, the peak amplitude of the current is 100/(50√2)=√2, and the phase is −15°−45°=−60°. Therefore the instantaneous current is i=√2sin(ωt−60°) A.
